subject: geography
chapter_title: Population Distribution, Density, Growth and Composition

concepts.title: Distribution and Density of India's Population
concepts.definition: India is the second most populous country with 1,210 million people (2011); its population is unevenly distributed, with density rising from sparse Aravalli and north-eastern hills to over a thousand persons per sq km in the northern plains, depending on terrain, climate, water and development.
concepts.key_idea: Dividing a state's population by its area in square kilometres gives its density in persons per sq km.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy201.txt distribution and density sections (2011 census figures)

how does terrain affect distribution
define population density with units

solution_steps.explain: density equals population divided by area

concepts.title: Phases of Population Growth
concepts.definition: India's population growth falls into four phases: the stagnant phase before 1921 with high mortality, the steadily expanding phase 1921-1951 (1921 as the year of great divide), the rapid high-growth phase 1951-1981, and the phase of high growth with definite signs of slowing since 1981.
concepts.key_idea: The death rate fell faster than the birth rate in every phase after 1921, which is why growth accelerated even as families shrank.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy201.txt growth phases and year of great divide sections
question_patterns: name the four phases of India's population growth

solution_steps.explain: 1921 separates the earlier mortality-dominated period from sustained expansion
stagnant, steady, rapid and slowing phases follow in order
birth-death differentials explain each phase's growth

concepts.title: Sex Ratio and Age Composition
concepts.definition: The sex ratio counts females per thousand males; India's 2011 census recorded 940 females per thousand males, with sharp interstate contrasts, while the age composition shows India as a young country with a large working-age share and a declining child share.
concepts.key_idea: Multiplying the female-male ratio by a thousand expresses the sex ratio conventionally as females per thousand males.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy201.txt sex ratio (940 in 2011) and age composition sections

solution_steps.explain: sex ratio is females per thousand males

concepts.title: Work Participation and Occupational Structure
concepts.definition: The work participation rate is the proportion of working population (workers) to total population; occupational structure divides workers into cultivators, agricultural labourers, household industry and other workers, and a high share of primary workers signals underemployment disguised in agriculture.
concepts.key_idea: Development shifts workers from primary to secondary and tertiary occupations, so occupational structure is a development indicator.
concepts.textbook_ref: legy201.txt work participation rate and occupational categories sections
question_patterns: define work participation rate

solution_steps.explain: workers as a proportion of total population is the participation rate
cultivators, agricultural labourers, household industry workers and other workers form the census classes
tertiary share rises as economies mature
